extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, attorneys/respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and USPTO/OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing imposition of reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including notice/service requirements, opportunity to respond, duties during suspension, and administrative consequences (publication, dissociation of customer numbers/PKI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may impose reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State (here, suspension for two years), pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order applies the State-imposed discipline to practice before the USPTO when appropriate; the Order states 'Respondent is hereby suspended for two (2) years ... for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).'

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds to oppose reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)) and deadline to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is provided an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the State based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file a timely response may result in a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d) and imposition of identical discipline; the Order notes Respondent did not file a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and publication of Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must attempt service of the Notice and Order (here sent by certified mail, with receipt number) and, if unsuccessful, publish the Notice and Order in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was sent by certified mail (receipt no. ...) and, after unsuccessful delivery attempts, published in the Official Gazette to effect notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of no genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response, the USPTO may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order: 'In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is hereby determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and Respondent's suspension ... is the appropriate discipline.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) (predicate suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action before the USPTO can be predicated upon a respondent being suspended from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State, constituting a violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice states the suspension is 'for violating 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being suspended from the practice of law for two years by a duly constituted authority of a State.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of disciplined practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: A disciplined respondent must comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifically directs 'Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58' (these duties include, for example, client notification, transfer of files, and notification to tribunals, as set forth in § 11.58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice of suspension and content of Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director will publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette identifying the respondent, registration number, scope of suspension (patent, trademark, other non-patent matters), the regulatory violation, and the underlying facts/reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample Notice of Suspension contains: respondent name and registration number, statement that suspension was ordered in a reciprocal proceeding, citation to 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), factual summary (e.g., failure to appear, failure to refund client, failure to communicate, CLE ineligibility), and reference to where disciplinary decisions are available (OED FOIA Reading Room URL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs the OED Director to 'give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59' of the discipline and reasons to the listed recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative/technical restrictions (dissociation of Customer Numbers and PKI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers; the respondent shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number or have their name added to one until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order instructs dissociation and bars any application for or addition to a USPTO Customer Number while suspended, effective until reinstatement to practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service and mailing requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Orders must be served (here mailed first class certified mail, return receipt requested) to the respondent at the address provided pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11, with a certificate of service filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document includes a 'CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE' certifying mailing of the Final Order to Respondent at the address provided pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of underlying misconduct supporting discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of the respondent's misconduct that supported the State suspension and thus the USPTO reciprocal discipline: failure to appear for imposition of an Informal Admonition, failure to refund client's monies, failure to participate in disciplinary process, failure to communicate with client, failure to notify client of ineligibility to practice after administrative suspension for failure to comply with CLE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice lists specific violations of Pennsylvania Rules of Professional Conduct (1.3, 1.4(a)(3), 1.4(a)(4), 1.4(b), 8.4(c)) and Pennsylvania Rules of Disciplinary Enforcement (203(b)(3) via 217(a), 217(j)(1), 217(j)(2), 217(j)(4)(ii)-(vi), and 203(b)(7)) as the factual basis for the State suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for USPTO disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions are taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 as the legal basis for imposing reciprocal discipline and publishing disciplinary decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice states: 'This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.' It also directs where disciplinary decisions are publicly available (OED FOIA Reading Room).
